Bank of America places holds on deposited checks to give the bank and the paying bank time to validate the check [2]. This helps protect you from potential fees if the check is returned unpaid.

Holds typically last 2–7 business days, depending on the reason [1]. You'll be notified of any hold through your deposit receipt, ATM screen, mobile app confirmation, or email/mail [4].

If you'd prefer to avoid holds altogether, Bank of America suggests asking those who pay you to use electronic methods instead—like direct deposit, ACH transfers, wire transfers, or Zelle®. These are usually available the same day [6].

results.answer:
When you deposit a check through the Mobile Banking app, funds are generally available the next business day [3]. Here's how it works:

- If you deposit before the cutoff time on a business day, Bank of America processes it that night and makes it available the next business day [3].
- Cutoff times depend on your time zone: before 9:00 p.m. ET (Eastern/Central) or before 8:00 p.m. MT/PT (Mountain/Pacific) [1].
- If you deposit after cutoff or on a weekend/holiday, it's processed the next business day and available the business day after that [3].

Bank of America may place a hold on some or all of the funds while validating the check [6], which could delay availability. To learn how to avoid holds, visit Bank of America's Deposit Holds FAQs [6].

  Tampa, FL 33622-5118

Before closing, Bank of America suggests [2] calling 800.432.1000 to discuss your account first.

**Before you close**, make sure to [3][4][6]:
- Bring your balance to zero by transferring it a few days ahead
- Update your mailing and email address (you'll get a final statement)
- Cancel recurring payments and stop new transactions
- Destroy debit cards and checks
- Download statements you need for your records

Bank of America charges overdraft fees when a transaction exceeds your available balance [4]. Here's why this might happen:

- Your available balance can drop due to transactions still processing. A pending purchase lowers what's available even before it posts to your account [5].
- Holds on your account also reduce your available balance [4].
- The order transactions post matters—a check might post before a purchase you made earlier [4].

To see exactly what happened, check your Account Details in Mobile and Online Banking to view posted transactions for that day. You can also look at Account Balance History in Online Banking to see how pending transactions and holds affected your available balance and caused the overdraft [4][5].

If you want to prevent overdrafts in the future, Bank of America offers settings to decline transactions when you lack funds, with no overdraft fees [2].
